# September 18, 2026

## Summary {.unnumbered}

- **A matched expression--methylation raw joint-YFB model is now implemented as an isolated module, with frozen prediction and matched-cohort simulations.** The established single-modality YFB production code is unchanged. (§1)
- **The raw multimodal parameterization required a numerical reparameterization.** Factor-scale canonicalization preserves fitted reconstructions and the raw predictor; convergence is now assessed with scale-invariant relative fitted changes. (§2)
- **A full-convergence $K_{\mathrm{init}}=5,\ldots,15$ screening panel confirms that active-factor counts cannot select rank.** The next selection stage is a paired replicated held-out evaluation. (§3)
- **The September 4 follow-up questions now have explicit status: Normal $\beta$ shrinkage and direct survival feedback are implemented; replicated K selection, prior sensitivity, and matched real cohorts remain open.** (§4)

---

## §1 — Matched multimodal YFB implementation

The new model follows the reviewed derivation in `derivations/multimodal_YFB/`.
Production helpers, preprocessing, updates, fitting, prediction, and simulation
live in `code/`; focused tests live in `tests/`. The model is intentionally
separate from the established single-mode YFB fitter.

For matched expression and methylation blocks,

$$
Y_m=LF_m^\top+E_m, \qquad
\eta_i=\sum_k\beta_k\sum_m\sum_jY_{mij}F_{mjk}.
$$

$L$ is a shared nonnegative score matrix, $F_m$ are modality-specific
nonnegative loading matrices, and both modalities retain separate loading
priors and feature precisions. Every $F_m$ update includes its reconstruction
term and its Cox-working-model contribution. This is the intended supervised
multimodal extension, not an unsupervised factorization followed by Cox
regression.

The simulation framework supplies independent matched training and validation
cohorts with proportional-hazards survival generated from the same raw joint
predictor. It compares joint multimodal YFB with unsupervised EBMF→Cox,
expression-only and methylation-only YFB, and a stacked-risk Cox baseline.
The full test harness passes (509/509), and all 35 derivation-algebra checks
pass. The planned formal multi-replicate K-selection study has not yet been
run.

## §2 — Resolving raw-scale convergence

The model has a factor-wise scale symmetry:

$$
(L_{\cdot k},F_{m\cdot k},\beta_k) \mapsto
(a_kL_{\cdot k},F_{m\cdot k}/a_k,a_k\beta_k),\qquad a_k>0.
$$

This transformation leaves both $LF_m^\top$ and the raw predictor $\eta$
unchanged. Initial fits could continue moving along this non-identifiable
direction despite stable fitted data and risk scores. The fitter now sets the
sample standard deviation of each factor's raw joint projection to one after
its coordinate update, transforming posterior second moments and
point-exponential prior rates consistently. This controls representation scale
without normalizing the predictor or removing survival feedback.

The stopping rule now tests the relative maximum change in each identifiable
fitted reconstruction and in $\eta$:

$$
\frac{\max|q^{(t)}-q^{(t-1)}|}
{\max\{1,\max|q^{(t)}|,\max|q^{(t-1)}|\}} < 10^{-4}.
$$

This is invariant to raw modality units. The initial 300-sweep cap was too
short for a stable K=7 draw (it required 314 sweeps), so the isolated
multimodal cap is 500. Raw latent moment change is retained as a diagnostic
but is not a valid convergence criterion under scale exchangeability. A
standardized Cox warm start prevents an all-zero coefficient fixed point, and
the point-exponential update handles subnormal zero-information floating-point
remainders explicitly.

These changes must be recorded in future methods writing: they choose a
numerical representative in an equivalent parameterization, rather than
changing the fitted likelihood or risk score.

## §3 — Preliminary K-init diagnostic

Following the single-mode broad sweep and its contiguous $10$--$15$
diagnostic, the multimodal model was fit at $K_{\mathrm{init}}=5,\ldots,15$
on the same both-informative simulation draw (seed 20260919; 120 training
and 120 validation patients; 50 features per modality). Every fit converged.

| $K_{\mathrm{init}}$ | Recon.-active | Survival-active | Union retained | Held-out C-index |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 5 | 1 | 5 | 0.734 |
| 6 | 6 | 1 | 6 | 0.732 |
| 7 | 6 | 1 | 6 | 0.777 |
| 8 | 7 | 2 | 7 | 0.744 |
| 9 | 6 | 5 | 9 | 0.749 |
| 10 | 6 | 4 | 9 | 0.747 |
| 11 | 6 | 4 | 8 | 0.743 |
| 12 | 9 | 3 | 9 | 0.792 |
| 13 | 7 | 3 | 8 | 0.759 |
| 14 | 7 | 6 | 10 | 0.712 |
| 15 | 9 | 3 | 9 | 0.784 |

The C-index and held-out partial likelihood peak at $K_{\mathrm{init}}=12$ in
this one draw, but this is **not** a selected default. Although the fits
converge numerically, marginal joint PVE $\geq1\%$ does not yield a
K-invariant effective count, and nominal survival flags increase at some higher
ranks. The K-selection runner therefore uses identical simulated training and
validation cohorts for every K within a replicate, checkpoints every fit, and
will select the smallest K within one standard error of the best mean held-out
C-index across independent replicates. Held-out partial likelihood is reported
as a secondary, same-risk-set diagnostic. Reconstruction-active,
survival-active, and union-retained counts remain separate outputs rather than
rank-selection rules.

### Adverse and protective program recovery

The new `adverse_protective` simulation sets the first two true joint programs
to $\beta=(0.70,-0.70,0)$, so successful recovery requires both retention and
the correct adverse/protective directions. At $K_{\mathrm{init}}=12$ on the
same held-out draw, the fit converged with six reconstruction-active, four
survival-active, and eight union-retained factors; it recovered both true
prognostic programs and both signs (prognostic and direction recall = 1.0).
The extra nominal survival factors are another reason the final rank must be
selected from repeated held-out performance, not coefficient flags alone.

### Reconstruction parsimony: tested and deferred extension

The current point-exponential priors shrink individual score and loading
coordinates; they are not a valid whole-factor ARD mechanism. A shared
Gamma-rate prototype was tested as a factor-level relevance parameter, but it
did not reduce the number of reconstruction-active factors and worsened
held-out C-index. It was removed rather than retained as a nominal ARD option.

Accordingly, reconstruction parsimony is currently obtained by externally
selecting $K_{\mathrm{init}}$ from paired replicated held-out performance,
then reporting the reconstruction/survival retention classes within that fit.
A future group spike-and-slab or group-penalty extension would require a new
derivation and its own recovery study; it is not part of the current method.

## §4 — Follow-up questions from the September 4 meeting

### Coefficient prior

The multimodal derivation uses a Normal (ridge-type) prior for $\beta$, which
has an exact conjugate update. This is consistent with single-mode YFB evidence
that a Normal prior is necessary when PDAC survival signal is weak; point-normal
shrinkage can collapse coefficients to zero in small folds. Laplace-prior
comparison remains a planned sensitivity analysis, not a current model change.

### Initialization, K selection, and factor retention

The fitter uses nonnegative-SVD initialization plus a Cox warm start. The
current K panel checks K sensitivity, not 100 random starts. Its initial result
shows that convergence alone is insufficient: marginal PVE reporting is not a
rank-selection method in this over-specified nonnegative factorization. The
next evidence must come from paired replicated held-out C-index and partial
likelihood, with the fixed-working objective kept as an optimization diagnostic.

### Supervision and low-variance prognostic factors

Unlike the single-mode compatibility implementation, survival directly enters
the multimodal loading update. A low-variance prognostic-factor scenario is
included to test whether this can retain clinical signal that is not dominant
in reconstruction. Prognostic activity is currently based on
$|E(\beta_k)|/\operatorname{SD}(\beta_k)\geq1.96$, which is invariant to the
factor-scale transformation. Relative-to-largest-$|\beta|$ thresholding remains
a simulation-only sensitivity analysis.

### Cohorts and future real data

No matched TCGA/ICGC expression--methylation cohorts are yet in scope, so no
cohort indicator or cohort-specific multimodal coefficient has been added. The
single-mode results caution that genomics-side cohort indicators can compete
with prognostic structure and apparent cohort-specific effects can reflect
limited sample size. A future cohort term must specify whether its factor is
fixed, whether its survival coefficient is constrained to zero, and how
survival comparability is checked.

## Next steps

1. Run the checkpointed paired $K_{\mathrm{init}}=5,\ldots,15$ panel over
   independent seeds and apply the pre-specified one-standard-error rule.
2. Refit the selected K and report reconstruction, survival, and union counts;
   do not substitute a marginal-PVE threshold for rank selection.
3. Run the approved smoke study only with converged controls and a defensible
   K-selection procedure.
4. Reconcile the scale-canonicalization note with the editable derivation
   source before writing manuscript methods.
